clue.text: Against having endless search for old objects

parts.note: against means anti, opposed to

indicators.note: endless says the word for search loses its final letter

parts.note: a search is a quest

explanation.surface: A collector declares opposition to a never-ending hunt for old things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from QUEST, leaving QUES, which follows ANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiques are collectible items made long ago, valued for their age.

clue.text: A symbol of Christian hope on the other side

parts.note: the cross is the central symbol of Christianity

explanation.surface: A crucifix represents faith on the far side.
explanation.definitionFit: Across means over to or on the far side, as across the street.

clue.text: Something used by boatman or farmer?

definitions.text: Something used by boatman or farmer?

parts.words: Something used by boatman or farmer?
parts.note: a steering lever in a small boat, and also a machine or person working the soil

explanation.walkthrough: The boat's steering bar and a farmer's soil-cultivating machine share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is steered by this lever, while a farmer's cultivating machine or one who ploughs is called the same.

clue.text: Unpleasant situation, as with nasty grime

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, meaning as

indicators.note: nasty means rough or messed up, so the letters of grime are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horrible state of affairs, with filthy dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns GRIME into GMIRE, which follows QUA.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is literally a bog, figuratively an awkward or tricky predicament.

clue.text: Despicable people decapitated fish

indicators.note: decapitated means beheaded, so the first letter of the word for despicable people goes

parts.note: heels are cads, contemptible people

explanation.surface: Contemptible folk behead some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the H from HEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Learned person made play on words for audience, being with it

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is heard spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: to make a play on words is to pun, so in the past tense punned
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar who cracked a joke for the listeners and was fashionable with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' makes PUNNED heard as PUND; 'being with' joins IT on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert or authority, originally a learned Hindu scholar.

clue.text: Take action when the case has opened

definitions.text: Take action when the case has opened

parts.words: Take action when the case has opened
parts.note: reads like a lawyer starting work on a trial, but means taking things out of a suitcase

explanation.surface: A lawyer swings into action once the trial is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: After a trip, a traveller empties a suitcase, taking out clothes and belongings.

clue.text: Performed outside that place and was trembling

indicators.note: outside means the word for performed goes round the word for that place

parts.note: performed means did, as in did a task
that place is there

explanation.surface: Someone did a show outdoors over there and shook with nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts DID round THERE: DI + THERE + D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithered means hesitated, and in older British use it meant trembled or quivered.

clue.text: Agreeing to meet, attempt to smart

parts.note: an attempt is a try
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Arranging a date, trying to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective about looking good, but it is the verb meaning hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' secret meeting, so arranging one is agreeing a rendezvous.

clue.text: Engineers apt to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
apt, as in likely to do something, means liable

explanation.surface: Army engineers are inclined to be dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable can be depended on, the meaning of trustworthy.

clue.text: Indifference means a course is taken with little yen

parts.note: a course or route is a path
little signals the abbreviation: Y is short for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: Not caring means someone follows a route with hardly any desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like longing, matching the surface, but here it is the currency, shortened to Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, the same as not caring.

clue.text: Fine food one Arab stored in hollow

indicators.note: stored in means placed inside the word for a hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock
the Roman numeral I is one
Ar. is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Delicacies kept by an Arab in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stored in' puts I + AR inside CAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, an older spelling, is sturgeon roe, a costly delicacy.

clue.text: Mates excited by victory finally like a bath

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the word Mates are rearranged
finally picks out the last letter of the word victory

explanation.surface: Team-mates thrilled by a win celebrate in a hot bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns MATES into STEAM; 'finally' adds the Y that ends 'victory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot bath fills the room with vapour, so it is described as full of moisture and heat.

clue.text: Sly direction given to hide funds for campaign

indicators.note: given to hide means the compass word is made to conceal another inside it

parts.note: west is a compass direction
arch means slyly knowing or mischievous

explanation.surface: A cunning instruction to conceal money for an election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to hide' puts ARCH inside WEST, splitting it as W + ARCH + EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is money set aside for a campaign, political or military.

clue.text: Fixed knocking sound inside snow vehicle

indicators.note: inside means the knock word sits within the word for a snow vehicle

parts.note: a sled is a sledge for snow
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: A rattle inside the sledge has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts TAP within SLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stapled means fastened with metal wire clips, so held in place.

clue.text: The country needs someone intelligent, it is admitted

indicators.note: is admitted means the word it is let inside the word for a clever person

parts.note: a clever person is called a brain
taken as written

explanation.surface: The nation needs a genius, and that is conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is admitted' puts IT inside BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is a nation in north-west Europe, the island holding England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Nitrogen, a long time recognised as an element

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
an eon is an immeasurably long period

explanation.surface: Nitrogen has long been accepted as one of the chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nitrogen' and 'element' both suggest chemistry, but nitrogen gives only its symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, number ten in the periodic table.

clue.text: Inhabitants, with just one man accepting a form of Buddhism

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the man's name holds the Buddhist term

parts.note: Denis is a man's name
Zen is a school of Buddhism stressing meditation

explanation.surface: Residents, only one of them a man, embrace a branch of Buddhism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts ZEN inside DENIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Denizens are residents or occupants of a place.

clue.text: One has the right to lead when there's a fight

definitions.text: One has the right to lead when there's a fight

parts.words: One has the right to lead when there's a fight
parts.note: a boxer who throws the leading punches with the right hand, being left-handed

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to take charge when a quarrel breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the right' looks like an entitlement but is the right hand, which a left-handed boxer leads with.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer stands with the right foot and fist forward.

clue.text: Someone in a tree?

parts.note: suggests a person up in branches, but means a forebear on a genealogical chart

explanation.definitionFit: A forebear appears on a family tree, the chart of one's lineage.

clue.text: A Greek god irritated when rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for irritated is read backwards

parts.note: irritated means sore, as in feeling aggrieved

explanation.surface: A deity from Greek myth is annoyed at being spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rejected' turns SORE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of love, the counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Economical supplier of water contacted by phone

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring supplying water
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A thrifty water company gets in touch by telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: RING is the British word for telephoning someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sparing means using little, so careful and frugal with resources.

clue.text: Stupid person not English — an old Scottish king

indicators.note: not means without, so the English abbreviation is left out of the word for a stupid person

parts.note: a dunce is a slow learner
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dimwit who is not English, a long-ago Scottish monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the E from DUNCE, leaving DUNC, before AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan I ruled Scotland in the eleventh century and was killed by Macbeth.

clue.text: Knight with a standard in combative sport

parts.note: K is an abbreviation for knight, as in KBE
a standard or level is a rate

explanation.surface: A knight with his banner joins a fighting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a knight's flag, but it means a rate or level.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed fighting.

clue.text: Artist tries to escape? Has to be caught

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so the word for escaping holds the other

parts.note: someone trying to escape runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter tries to flee but has to be captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts BE inside RUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: Unwelcome guest? I turn red, being put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so the letters of I turn red are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has turned up uninvited blushes with embarrassment at being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put out' looks like the blushing guest's embarrassment, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters where not invited, so the question mark marks a playful description of one.

clue.text: Uncanny experience that makes Dave and June not half confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are shuffled together
not half means only the first half of the word June is kept

explanation.surface: Dave and June feel bewildered by a strange feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps JU from June; with DAVE that is DAVEJU, and 'confused' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deja vu is the eerie sense of having lived through a present moment before.

clue.text: Energy exuded by loud trading-station

indicators.note: exuded means given off, so the energy letter leaves the musical word

parts.note: forte is the musical term for loud
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Power pours out of a noisy trading post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exuded' drops the E from FORTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort was a fortified trading post, as in Hudson's Bay Company outposts.

clue.text: Suppose old flame will get kissed audibly

parts.note: an old flame, a former partner, is an ex

indicators.note: audibly means the word is to be heard, so a sound-alike spelling is used

parts.note: a quick kiss is a peck, so kissed is pecked

explanation.surface: Presumably a former lover will be heard getting a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns PECKED into PECT, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to think it likely, to presume or reckon.

clue.text: Snake track — a challenge for Oxbridge types

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
to track something is to trace it

explanation.surface: Following a snake's trail is a test for Oxford and Cambridge students.
explanation.walkthrough: The BOAT RACE is the annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge universities on the Thames; 'Oxbridge' blends the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowing contest is a yearly contest between crews from the two ancient English universities.

clue.text: Domestic activity in south-east part of the house

parts.note: a wing is a section of a large house

explanation.surface: Household chores happen in one corner of a mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching clothes and mending is a traditional household task.

clue.text: Course officials at Cheltenham and Aintree?

definitions.text: Course officials at Cheltenham and Aintree?

parts.words: Course officials at Cheltenham and Aintree?
parts.note: officials on a racecourse who get the horses away; Course also hints at the first dish of a meal

explanation.surface: Racecourse staff at two famous English horse-racing venues.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham and Aintree are famous English racecourses; 'Course' also suggests the first dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: At a race meeting the officials who signal the off are so called, as are opening dishes of a meal.
